intro:
derio-net/super-fr · fr 5.0.1 · origin/main 393b0278 · refreshed 2026-10-02 · after the talk · take 12 done

super-fr then and now, with every open defect pinned where it lives

The talk is done, and nothing has merged since 5.0.1 on 2026-09-29. Waves 1 to 9 and the cut (5.0.0, #851) are behind us: the operator removed the input layer, so the spec is now the contract and a requirement the spec omits is a spec defect. Take 12 ran on 5.0.0 and passed all four criteria of the new contract (#853) in 32.0 minutes for $3.50, against 42.5 minutes and $5.13 for the previous light-path run on the same brief. No plain-agent run was set beside it, so the light path's 2× benchmark row is still open. Against the plain baseline implied by the 4.40.0 result (2.41× cost and 3.32× time at $5.13 and 42.5 minutes), take 12 is about 1.6× on cost and 2.5× on time, inside the target on cost and on its edge on time: an inference from two single runs, not a measurement. Take 12 also hit the one defect 5.0.0 shipped with, a hardcoded plan ceiling that refused every plan the new fr wrote. 5.0.1 (#856) fixed the ceiling, and #854 and #855 are what that failure left. This page now ends with the order for closing the backlog: 85 open issues, of which 53 defects and follow-ups fit in twelve batches over three waves, then six ranked groups of features.

Wave 1 · 2026-09-26 → 27 · measured

Five batches merged; one blanket model made them slower and more expensive than they had to be

Every wave-1 batch was dispatched with --model claude-sonnet-5, copied from batch to batch by the agent that created them. The brief turns that value into "use it for every subagent and every model tier", so the orchestrator, executors and reviewers all ran on Sonnet, overriding the configured bindings (orchestrator and hard on Opus, standard on Sonnet, mechanical on Haiku). Four sessions blocked before the end. The operator then had every review re-run on Opus as a one-off. Those Opus reviews surfaced most of the issues filed since, #705 and #716 among them. #704 tracks the fix: start the session on the orchestrator binding and let the tiers resolve.

relay:
5.0.0 · #851 · the operator's decision after take 10's live walk

The brief grew four gates and a reviewer; 5.0.0 took them out

#762 (4.29.0) stored the operator's brief verbatim and required every requirement to quote it. That was the right first step. Each live run then found the next place the brief could be lost, and each fix added another reader of it: a grammar, a coverage partition, a fidelity check, a requirement-rows gate, an agent that fetches the input for the code review, and three journal tokens to record who answered what. Take 10 showed the result on OpenCode: the gates passed with a made-up reviewer. The operator's conclusion was that the input feeds the brainstorm and nothing else. If the spec did not capture it, it is not implemented; if the spec is wrong, nothing downstream can fix it.
